notes: 10-04 12:56 READY on lane/m1-durable: fn-lgu-take-verdict (books/store-log-durable.lisp) asked by host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-take-verdict before fnn-log-publish fences and before fnn-log-write-history's take; fn-lgu-host-records-p removed from the keystone; certify-20261004T165405Z-4135. Native red/green not built (no shipped profile reaches the window); the ACL2 teeth are the red/green.
title: The log takes records its scan cannot read back: fnn-log-publish admits a record of at most R octets (fn-store-publication-admissibility: length <= the profile's max_record_octets R), fn-olr-take checks no framing bound, and the scan opens a one-record entry with payload bound R (fn-lg-open-bound), whose payload is the 32-octet chain then the record; a record of R-31..R octets is appended, fenced and acknowledged, and the next open stops at its entry and zeroes it and every later record (P-LOG-RECOVER). PRF-936's keystone carries fn-lgu-host-records-p (fn-lg-recordp at R) for exactly this and no host theorem discharges it; the teeth witness (tests/acl2/store-log-durable-tests.lisp, 4070 octets at R=4096) shows the loss. Unreachable in the shipped presets (R far above A plus the header limit), reachable only for a profile whose R is within 32 octets of its largest record. Fix: ACL2 decides the take's framing bound (fn-lg-recordp of the record the log takes at fnn-store-log-max, a named refusal before the store is fenced; fnn-log-write-history's import too), with a theorem that discharges fn-lgu-host-records-p on the host path
